// Module
var code = `<h1>Response format</h1> <p>The response format determines which capabilities the AI provider must support for extra-model parsing and how reliably MVU can read the variable updates.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Chat message:</strong> Offers the widest compatibility and requires no additional provider features. Reliability depends on whether the model follows the requested format.</li> <li><strong>Tool call:</strong> Requires tools/function-calling support. It usually reduces interference from prose, but unsupported models or reverse proxies may fail or degrade.</li> <li><strong>Structured output:</strong> Requires OpenAI-compatible <code>response_format.json_schema</code> support. This is usually the best option for JsonPatch variable updates because the response is constrained to structured JSON.</li> <li><strong>Structured output (v4 compatible):</strong> For providers, such as dsv4f, that support only <code>response_format.type = json_object</code>. This mode is available only when the extra-model source is <strong>Custom</strong>.</li> </ul> <p>If your provider explicitly supports <code>response_format.json_schema</code>, try <strong>Structured output</strong> first. Otherwise, use <strong>Structured output (v4 compatible)</strong> or <strong>Chat message</strong>. You can also try <strong>Tool call</strong> when the provider supports tools/function calling.</p> `;
// Exports
export default code;
