// Module
var code = `<h1>Request method</h1> <h2>How do the methods differ?</h2> <h3>Request sequentially and retry on failure</h3> <p>This works much like asking the AI to regenerate an unsatisfactory story reply:</p> <ul> <li>Send one request to the AI.</li> <li>If the reply contains variable-update commands, apply them.</li> <li>Otherwise, keep requesting until the configured number of requests is reached.</li> </ul> <h3>Send multiple requests in parallel</h3> <p>This method sends the configured number of requests <strong>at the same time</strong>:</p> <ul> <li>Send as many simultaneous requests as the “Number of requests” setting specifies.</li> <li>As soon as one reply contains variable-update commands, apply it and cancel the other unfinished requests.</li> </ul> <p>This reduces waiting time, but parallel requests consume additional tokens. For models such as Claude that bill with prompt caching, you can also use the method below.</p> <h3>Request once, then retry in parallel on failure</h3> <p>Send one request first. If it fails, send multiple requests in parallel.</p> <h2>When should I use parallel requests?</h2> <p>If your model's requests-per-minute (RPM) limit is high enough, use “Send multiple requests in parallel” or “Request once, then retry in parallel on failure.”</p> <h2>Do parallel requests waste many tokens?</h2> <p>Usually not. Extra-model parsing uses only:</p> <ul> <li>World-book entries whose names contain <code>[mvu_update]</code>;</li> <li>World-book entries whose names contain neither <code>[mvu_plot]</code> nor <code>[mvu_update]</code>;</li> <li><strong>Only the last two chat messages</strong>;</li> <li>Preset prompts, if a preset is being sent.</li> </ul> <p>Chat history usually accounts for most token usage in SillyTavern, while extra-model parsing reads only the last two messages. With a sensibly designed character-card world book, batch requests generally do not waste many tokens.</p> `;
// Exports
export default code;
